incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egypt Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Articles 8-31 (LLC provisions) and related implementing regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry and Investor Services Center
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notarized Memorandum/Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Egyptian law, but the company must maintain capital adequate to achieve its stated objects; for a retail e-commerce entity a subscribed paid-up capital of at least EGP 50,000 is recommended, paid into a temporary bank escrow account before registration and released after incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers' subscription of the share capital of EG_LLC, allocated as specified in the Memorandum and Articles of Association, be and is hereby accepted and confirmed. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be situated at the address stated in the Articles of Association, and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones be notified accordingly. RESOLVED that the first directors and officers of the Company be and are hereby appointed, including the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next ordinary general assembly and to exercise all powers conferred by the Companies Law and the Articles of Association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center / GAFI Electronic Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name reservation application through the GAFI e-portal specifying the preferred corporate name EG_LLC and three alternate names. Pay the name reservation fee, submit the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association, and obtain a formal name availability certificate before proceeding with incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport copies of all shareholders and managers
Registered office lease contract or declaration of domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or prohibited use, file an administrative objection with the GAFI Name Committee within 15 calendar days and resubmit with two alternative names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Bank Escrow Arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Bank (conforming to Central Bank of Egypt regulations) and Public Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the proposed company name at an Egyptian bank and deposit the subscribed capital. Obtain a bank certificate confirming the deposit, then have all shareholders execute their subscription signatures before a Notary Public or GAFI certification officer.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for any representative signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the pre-registration escrow account due to absence of a commercial register number, request a provisional account eligibility letter from GAFI and complete the bank's KYC remediation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation File to GAFI Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed and notarized Articles of Association, escrow certificate, registered office documentation, and all supporting IDs to the GAFI One-Shop desk. Require the legal inspector to review conformity with the Companies Law and then issue the Certificate of Incorporation and commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office lease contract or ownership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a substantive query regarding the objects clause or capital adequacy, respond through the appointed legal counsel within 10 working days, filing a supplementary notarized amendment if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Issuance of Tax Card
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority - Local State Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the commercial registration extract and incorporation certificate to the competent Egyptian Tax Authority office using the standard tax card application form. Appoint the tax representative, provide the board resolution, and obtain the tax card and provisional tax identification number for income tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry extract and certificate of incorporation
First board resolution appointing tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card is delayed beyond the service standard, file a written escalation with the Tax Authority Customer Service Center and, if necessary, submit a formal complaint to the ETA head office after 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration and Payment Rails Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority - VAT Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for VAT under Egyptian Value Added Tax Law No. 67 of 2016 within the applicable threshold timeline. Complete the VAT registration form describing online retail of consumer electronics and smart gadgets, submit projected revenues and bank details, and obtain the VAT registration certificate.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form and supporting schedules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT application is queried due to incomplete revenue projections, provide a sales forecast and, where applicable, obtain an administrative rating decision determining VAT filing obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance and Corporate Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Managers / LLC General Assembly, Public Notary, and Corporate Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, open the corporate bank account in the name of EG_LLC using the commercial registry extract, tax card, and board resolution, and arrange for the corporate seal to be engraved and manager signatures to be certified by the bank.
required_dossiers: Passports and signature specimens of authorized managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial ownership declarations or rejects the corporate account, complete the electronic KYC declaration and, where needed, seek mediation through the Central Bank of Egypt Banking Ombudsman.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - non-industrial, non-manufacturing e-commerce business; no manufacturing permit is required under the Egyptian Industrial Licensing Law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for online retail activity; a municipal commercial license may apply only if a physical showroom or warehouse is established

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - not applicable unless a physical warehouse exceeds environmental screening thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no formal EIA required for pure online retail; registration may be triggered for storage facilities over 250 square meters)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Pursuant to Waste Management Law No. 182 of 2020, packaging waste must be segregated and disposed of through authorized municipal or licensed recyclers; no VOC or wastewater discharge thresholds apply to e-commerce operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate is required for any leased office or warehouse, along with structural load clearance for storage areas and Ministry of Labor occupational safety clearance for employees

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA - Maslahat al-Dara'ib al-Misriyyah), Cairo; e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipt platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; business registration through GAFI One-Stop-Shop: https://www.gafi.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned EG LLC: (1) incorporate via GAFI/Commercial Registry and obtain the Commercial Registry Extract (sak al-tagheel) plus the published Official Gazette notice; (2) file the ETA tax registration kit within 60 days of commercial establishment: authenticated Articles of Association, Commercial Registry Extract, board resolution appointing the director(s), passports and valid residence proof for managers/shareholders, notarized power of attorney (if remote) and the Egyptian office lease title; (3) ETA issues the unified 9-digit TIN, which is concurrently the corporate income tax, VAT and withholding tax registration number, and issues the Tax Card (validity subject to ETA renewal policy); (4) onboard the mandatory E-Invoicing / E-Receipt API with the ETA digital-certificate enrolment; (5) complete the social-insurance registration. Non-resident e-commerce vendors without an Egyptian branch are still obliged to register for VAT only, through the ETA remote non-resident registration module, appoint an Egyptian tax agent or fiscal intermediary (Exec. Reg. No. 66/2017, Arts. 30-31) and use the issued VAT TIN for e-invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate check-the-box or hybrid-entity elections: an LLC is irrevocably treated as a resident entity-level taxpayer under Law No. 91/2005. Available statutory mechanisms: (a) Free-zone/special-zone regime approved by GAFI under Law No. 72/2017 - exempts export-oriented free-zone profits from CIT and grants VAT customs treatment, but local-market retail sales remain fully taxable; (b) MSME presumptive taxation under Law No. 152/2020 - an eligible small LLC may elect the ETA-approved simplified fixed-margin tax basis in lieu of accounting profits; (c) investment incentive certificates for qualifying industrial/logistics projects in underdeveloped or economic zones - not generally available to pure online retailers; (d) accelerated depreciation under Art. 47 of Law 91/2005; (e) foreign hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralized by the non-deductibility of payments to preferential-regime jurisdictions (Art. 66 of Law 91/2005) and by treaty substance-over-form tests. Consolidation/fiscal unity is not permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Law No. 67 of 2016 (as amended), Executive Regulations Decree No. 66 of 2017; administered by the VAT sector of the ETA; applies to all taxable supplies of goods and services in Egypt plus imports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover for domestic businesses (Law 67/2016, Art. 29). No threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of digital/electronic-commerce services: VAT registration is compulsory from the first supply to an Egyptian consumer, regardless of turnover (Art. 30 and Exec. Reg. Art. 30).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance: all registered taxpayers must integrate through the ETA E-Invoicing API (JSON/XML schema with certified digital signatures), transmit invoices and B2C e-receipts for central validation prior to issuance, and print the ETA-generated UUID and QR stamp on the final fiscal document. Rollout is phased by turnover tiers; merchants selling through Stripe/PayPal must still generate and transmit a QR-coded Arabic e-receipt for each Egyptian consumer purchase in real time. Non-compliance results in suspension of the Tax Card, blocking of customs ACI privileges, and administrative fines of EGP 20,000-50,000 per violating transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) export of goods where the buyer is a non-resident, title passes to the buyer, and the goods physically leave the Egyptian customs territory within 90 days of the export invoice date (ETA extension possible); (2) services to non-resident persons where the benefit is used wholly abroad and the service is directly linked to exported goods (Exec. Reg. Art. 53); and (3) supplies to licensed free-zone projects confirmed by Egyptian Customs. Producers and merchants must mark the export invoice in the E-Invoicing system with export type code 'EX'; the claim fails if goods are diverted to the local market. A licensed online consumer-electronics exporter retains full input-VAT recovery attributable to the export sales, but pure domestic B2C sales remain taxable at 14%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Single Administrative Document (SAD) / electronic Export Declaration through ASYCUDA and the Advance Cargo Information (ACI) system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the export shipment and destination outside Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) / Foreign Exchange Transfer Certificate issued by an Egyptian authorized bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
QR-validated zero-rated export invoice issued through the ETA E-Invoicing system (export type code 'EX')
Signed export contract or foreign purchase order and corresponding payment evidence
Customs packing list and HS/ECC classification certificate for consumer electronics
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA, the Egyptian Customs Authority and the CBE exchange ACI/ASYCUDA, e-invoice and banking data to corroborate each export zero-rating claim, including physical exit, buyer residency and repatriation of hard currency within the 180-day CBE deadline. A false export declaration is VAT evasion under the penalty provisions of Law No. 67/2016: imprisonment up to five years and a fine between EGP 100,000 and EGP 1,000,000 (or not less than twice the tax evaded), together with mandatory restitution of the refund plus CBE credit-rate interest, and delay penalties of 2% per month (capped at 100%). The ETA may open and retroactively claw back refunds within the five-year assessment window; the exporter carries the full burden of proof. Repeated violations trigger cancellation of VAT registration, revocation of the e-invoice 'EX' privilege, customs export blacklisting and referral to public prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole regulator of banks, foreign-exchange operations, and payment systems under Law No. 194 of 2020; the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) administers FDI registration and capital-formation documentation for Egyptian LLCs; the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) issues the tax-clearance certificates that condition any outward foreign-currency remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the March 2024 flotation, the EGP is a market-determined, broadly convertible currency for current-account flows, including e-commerce receivables, import payments, commissions, royalties, and ordinary profit remittances, all handled through CBE-licensed banks without quotas or surrender certificates. Capital-account flows (equity injection, shareholder loans) require bank-level CDD, GAFI/BoP coding, and underlying documentation, but no separate CBE approval is required for an LLC's share-capital deposit. The practical hurdles are documentary: (i) no outward profit remittance is executed without the ETA income-tax clearance and tax card; (ii) import settlements require the Commercial Register, tax card, and GOEIC importer-eligibility file; (iii) any non-bank PSP (Stripe/PayPal) collection must be swept into the licensed bank to be recognized as statutory repatriation; (iv) financial statements must follow EAS/IFRS and reflect the BoP classification of all cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egyptian exporters, including cross-border e-commerce sellers, must repatriate the full invoice value through an authorized bank within four months of the shipping date per successive CBE foreign-exchange circulars; the proceeds must be credited to a CBE-bank account, and any receivable held in a foreign PSP wallet or offshore bank materially violates this repatriation duty. The compulsory EGP-conversion share historically applied to export proceeds (about 50%) was suspended under the March 2024 flexible-exchange-rate instruction, so the EG_LLC may retain export receipts in USD/EUR and convert at the interbank rate when funding import payables. For a predominantly import-based retail legal entity, the repatriation obligation is triggered only when the company resells cross-border; for import purchases the bank applies the reverse documentary discipline, verifying settlement against pro forma invoices, customs declarations, and the importer's GOEIC status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Egypt (NBE) S.A.E. — Cairo
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (share-capital subscription) + EGP operational current account + USD current account
Capital Escrow Account + EGP/USD operational settlement accounts for trade and PSP sweeps
EGP/USD operational current accounts + trade-finance and LC desk; capital deposit can be housed at the same branch under the GAFI formation flow
EGP/USD current accounts with international trade-services desk (MT103, MT700) for import-heavy treasury
EGP/USD operational accounts for e-commerce cash management and merchant-card acquiring settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury layer, AUXILIARY only for B2C collection. Legal constraints: CBE Law No. 194 of 2020 and the Egyptian Payments Law No. 18 of 2019 reserve account-keeping, clearing, and issuance of e-money to CBE-licensed banks and licensed PSPs; offshore digital EMIs (Stripe, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer) are not licensed in Egypt, cannot open EGP accounts, cannot be designated as a repatriation bank, and any proceeds resting in an EMI wallet are not recognized as statutory receipt. Stripe does not currently onboard Egyptian-domiciled merchants; PayPal is only a limited receive/withdrawal channel in Egypt and cannot provide settlement rails. Consequently, the EG_LLC must use a CBE-licensed local acquiring bank/PSP (e.g., CIB merchant services, NBE gateway, Paymob, Fawry, Telda) for card settlement, and any PayPal/Stripe-adjacent international collection must be swept daily to the licensed EGP/USD account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is the mandatory baseline under the CBE AML/CDD regime (Law No. 80 of 2002 and the CBE's Money-Laundering and Terrorist-Financing control instructions). The LLC's director(s), all UBOs at or above the bank's disclosure threshold (typically 10% or more, in practice 25%+ enforced), and authorized signatories must attend a physical compliance interview at the Egyptian branch and execute documents with wet-ink signatures; remote video-KYC alone is not accepted for a corporate current account. Non-resident shareholders can pre-verify documents abroad (notarized and consular-legalized by the Egyptian embassy/consulate) and may grant a local power-of-attorney, but at least one authorized natural person must appear in Egypt to complete the interview. Banks such as NBE's foreign-investment desk and CIB's priority unitsoffer a concierge path, but there is no fully remote opening route for a non-resident-owned Egyptian LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and corporate-chain opacity — the bank flags or delays the account where the non-resident shareholder is a holding vehicle or the individual UBO lacks a verifiable commercial track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO schedule (names, DOB, nationality, passport copies, exact shareholding percentages); certified extract of the LLC from the Egyptian Commercial Registry and GAFI file; notarized partners'/directors' resolution authorizing the account and its signatories; corporate-ownership chart; apostilled/consular-legalized constitutional documents of any corporate shareholder; signed CBE-compliant CDD forms; and a sanctions-screening certificate for all UBOs from a recognized screening provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency for the foreign-capital injection — EDD is triggered when the inbound USD share-capital wire cannot be linked to provable business earnings or accumulated wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month original bank statements of the remitting shareholder; SWIFT MT103 and credit advice evidencing the specific transfer; the LLC's share-subscription or contribution agreement; the shareholder's tax-residence certificate and filed tax returns (or audited financial statements if a corporate shareholder); a written source-of-wealth narrative supported by asset documents (sale deeds, dividend vouchers, inheritance instruments).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce and PSP risk indicators — the bank regards Stripe/PayPal-style B2C cross-border volumes as unexplained digital turnover, raising AML suspicion of smurfing, fraud, or trade mis-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company's banking AML-risk self-assessment reflecting the Low-Risk Standard tier; verified domain and marketplace ownership; platform payout statements exported from the PSP dashboards; supplier contracts and pro forma invoices; refund/chargeback policy with historical dispute ratios; GOEIC import-entry and customs documentation for the underlying consumer-electronics inventory; and a sworn undertaking to route all treasury movements exclusively through the licensed bank and to respect CBE cash-transaction thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and name-screening false hits — automated screening matches a UBO or counterparty against a common Arabic name or a de-listed entity with similar text in OFAC/UN/EU lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent screening printouts for every UBO and counterparty (World-Check or equivalent); official passport and national-ID copies; negative-media and PEP search results; a notarized sworn declaration of non-affiliation with sanctioned persons or entities; a banking referee letter from the UBO's home jurisdiction; and completed CBE due-diligence questionnaires demonstrating the basis of rebuttal.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: (1) execute the LLC's constitutive instrument and complete GAFI pre-registration; (2) open the share-capital escrow/subscription account at the chosen CBE-licensed bank presenting the Commercial-Registry extract and the partners' resolution; (3) the non-resident shareholder's overseas bank sends a SWIFT MT103 (USD/EUR) to the Egyptian bank's USD-correspondent clearing chain (e.g., beneficiary BIC CIBEEGCX for CIB, NBEGEGCX for NBE), naming the beneficiary precisely as 'EG_LLC' and stating the payment purpose in field 70 as 'Direct investment — share capital injection into Egyptian LLC'; (4) the receiving bank applies CDD to the remitter and records the BoP item 'Direct Investment / Equity'; (5) upon credit and any agreed EGP conversion at the interbank rate, the bank issues a capital-deposit certificate evidencing the paid share capital; (6) the LLC completes final GAFI registration and reflects the deposit in annual financial statements. Cash deliveries, third-party intermediary wiring without corporate-name identity, and unlicensed PSP wallets are not acceptable for the capital-formation route. Any inbound shareholder loan instead of equity must be booked through the bank, coded as 'Direct Investment / Debt', and is subject to Egyptian thin-cap and interest-withholding rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Import settlement rails for consumer-electronics purchases: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers from the company's USD account for advance-payment or documents-against-payment terms — accepted under the post-2023 relaxed regime provided the bank holds the pro forma invoice, the supplier's GOEIC registration proof, and the company's tax card, and the disbursement is filed against the import ledger; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit via SWIFT MT700 (issuance) and MT707 (amendment) for batch wholesale purchases, typically payable at sight against shipping documents and settled through the Egyptian bank's trade desk under the CBE import-documents verification framework; (iii) documentary collections (D/P or D/A) reintroduced in 2023 as a permitted alternative. For local Egyptian suppliers, disbursements use the CBE-operated national RTGS/ACH clearing rails. All outbound USD wires require linkage to the importer's Commercial Register, tax card, GOEIC registration, and eventual customs clearance; speculative overnight EGP/USD positioning by corporates is not permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP FX forwards, purchased USD vs EGP, executed directly with a CBE-licensed corporate bank against documented import exposure (pro forma invoice or LC); tenors generally 1–12 months, extendable toward 24 months with bank credit approval and initial margin/collateral of 10–15% of notional.

Offshore USD/EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only through the Egyptian bank's parent/affiliate for non-deliverable hedging of the EGP leg; permitted solely against genuine underlying commercial flows, never for speculative positions, and disfavored after the 2024 float in favor of the cheaper deliverable onshore market.

USD/EGP cross-currency swaps and FX swaps, executed on bank treasury approval to align the currency and tenor of import payables with EGP current-account revenues, supported by written trade contracts and cash-flow projections.

Purchased (long) USD-call/EGP-put options for hedging the e-commerce import-payment stream, available from major onshore banks where the option premium is economically justified; writing or selling options is not granted to standard retail trade corporates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Consolidated Revenue Return under State Revenue Law No. 4 of 2024) with audited balance sheet and income statement annexed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance - e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four months after the end of the fiscal year; 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 2% per month on unpaid tax (minimum EGP 100, maximum EGP 1,000 per month), fixed late-submission fines, suspension of the unified tax card, forced collection, and blocking of e-invoicing and customs privileges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and auditor's report deposited in the corporate file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - electronic company file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 4-month statutory window as the income tax return; copy filed within 30 days after the partners' approval meeting, which must occur no later than 6 months after the year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI non-compliance notice, administrative fines up to EGP 20,000, suspension of corporate e-services, and administrative strike-off after two consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Commercial Registration, Ministry of Trade and Industry, through GAFI one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the commercial registration date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Invalidates the operating licence, blocks bank facility and customs clearance, triggers late-renewal penalties, and may lead to deletion of the commercial register record

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Trade and municipal premises licence renewal, with civil defence fire-safety certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Governorate Trade Licensing Directorate and General Administration of Civil Defence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 December for the following business year, aligned with the commercial register renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Premises closure order, administrative closure, fines under Law No. 371 of 1956 (EGP 500 to 5,000), and suspension of e-invoicing address verification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual real beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation and UBO register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI - Beneficial Ownership Register; data available to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit upon inquiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 6 months of the fiscal year-end, aligned with GAFI data confirmation and audited statement filing; re-filing within 30 days of any quota transfer or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 100,000, criminal liability for false UBO disclosure, freezing of bank accounts by the AML unit, and denial of GAFI corporate services

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Unified tax card registration data confirmation and re-issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any registration data change; renewal at validity-cycle dates set by the ETA under State Revenue Law No. 4 of 2024; data confirmation performed with each annual return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Invalid tax card suspends e-invoicing enrolment, VAT recovery, and import/export privileges, with daily administrative penalties under Law No. 4 of 2024

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every Egyptian LLC regardless of capital, revenue, or headcount: Companies Law No. 163 of 2023 requires appointment of one or more certified auditors registered on the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) auditors' ledger, and the Egyptian Tax Authority requires the audited financial statements to be annexed to the annual income tax return; e-commerce retail additionally requires digital revenue and payment-rail reconciliation by the auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance, converged with IFRS; revenue from online retail recognized per EAS 17 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers), financial instruments per EAS 48, and presentation in EGP; IFRS as issued by the IASB is accepted only as supplementary or consolidated reporting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the AML Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) and GAFI Beneficial Ownership Regulations, the LLC must identify the natural person(s) directly or indirectly owning or controlling 10% or more of the quota capital (or otherwise exercising control), keep the UBO register at the registered office, file the annual UBO confirmation with GAFI during the annual data confirmation cycle, and re-file within 30 days of any quota transfer or change in control; the register must be produced to the AML unit, tax auditors, and competent authorities on demand
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Quota-Holders Register) with share transfer history
Register of Managers, signatory powers, and powers of attorney
General Assembly and Managers' minute book (partners' resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard LLC CIT is 22.5%. Investment Law 72/2017 may grant a 30%-50% investment allowance or up to 50% CIT reduction for qualifying projects in priority areas; Free Zone/SCZone licensed entities may obtain a 5-year income-tax holiday. E-commerce retail is not separately exempt and should not rely on a holiday without GAFI/ETA approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 8) submitted through Egyptian Tax Authority e-filing portal (www.eta.gov.eg); non-residents use the branch file and same form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, supported by quarterly estimated CIT instalments for established taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return and payment are due within four months after close of the taxable year; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April. Amended returns may be filed before assessment only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate original/amended filing, taxable year beginning and ending dates, previous ETA file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the PE/branch of a foreign LLC, state the Egyptian PE period and the ETA branch file number; if the foreign company has no PE, no Form 8 filing is required but domestic-source payments are subject to withholding by the payer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form (LLC), commercial registration number, unified tax number, address, capital and directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian branch name and address, not the foreign head office; attach the branch registration and tax card. Add the foreign parent name, country of incorporation and UBO details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C – Business Activity and Licenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare primary ISIC code and online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets; no statutory business license, but e-commerce platform merchant registrations should be stated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the activities actually performed in Egypt through employees, servers, warehouses or logistics; disclose a permanent establishment risk if sales contracts are concluded from Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net revenue from Stripe/PayPal, card and cash-on-delivery sales, cost of goods sold, fulfilment and marketing overhead, depreciation, financial charges, net accounting profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Egypt GAAP financial statements for the PE only, with intercompany revenue/expense eliminations; if management fees, royalties or interest are paid, attach contracts and evidence of arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses: penalties, bribes, excessive depreciation, excess interest, donations above quota, TP adjustment disallowed portions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter adjustments relating to Egyptian-source revenue allocated by treaty rules; when foreign head-office costs are recharged, ensure they are specifically identifiable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior tax losses applied not exceeding five years, foreign tax credit, investment allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs may offset only losses incurred in Egypt against Egyptian taxable income; no group relief except as expressly approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, CIT at 22.5%, advance instalments, final balance payable/payable refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branch profits are taxed at the same 22.5% rate; payment must be from the Egyptian branch bank account, not a foreign account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: TP declaration for transactions with related parties, including aggregate values, nature of transactions and transfer-pricing method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned LLC should attach Local File, Master File and country-by-country position when group thresholds are met; identify remuneration for functions actually performed in Egypt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed monetary fine per return, a tax card suspension risk, and late-payment surcharge of 2% per month on the unpaid CIT, capped at 100% of the tax. Underassessment caused by fraud adds criminal fine and imprisonment. The ETA may use estimated assessment charges if Form 8 is not submitted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; Egyptian resident corporate shareholders may benefit from participation exemption conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its tax authority, attach a Form of DTA application with the shareholding proof and beneficial ownership declaration, and submit these to the ETA before or on the distribution date. Approved relief is reflected in the withholding certificate; without ETA approval the payer withholds at the 10% statutory rate and a refund claim may be pursued later. Egypt applies a principal-purpose test so a shell shareholder lacking substance will be denied treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 20% for royalties and 20% for interest paid to non-resident recipients. Treaty rates in Egypt's DTAs commonly reduce royalties to 5%-15% and interest to 10%-15%, subject to beneficial ownership. For an Egyptian LLC buying consumer electronics IP or paying intercompany deferred-purchase interest, the rate should be analysed treaty-by-treaty and substantiated in Box H.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8 million aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers mandatory TP Disclosure Form and Local File; group consolidated turnover above EGP 500 million also requires Master File and CbCR positions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not run a separate ESR notification system, but the ETA enforces substance through GAAR, beneficial ownership rules and business-purpose doctrines. Free-zone/SCZone concessions require actual employees, premises, books and decision-making in Egypt. A shell Egyptian LLC interposed between offshore suppliers and consumers, holding only the e-commerce contract while all real functions are performed abroad, will be disregarded or recharacterised, with profits reassessed at the Egyptian level and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately excluding Stripe/PayPal payouts and cash-on-delivery revenue from Box D, overstating related-party supply invoices, or maintaining undisclosed foreign settlement accounts for an e-commerce LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional CIT assessment, late-payment surcharge at 2% per month capped at 100%, criminal fine up to EGP 20,000 or three times the evaded tax, imprisonment up to five years, and cancellation/renewal denial of the tax card.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the UBO who signed or caused the false return can be prosecuted jointly; courts may pierce the LLC veil and impose civil restitution, asset freezing and travel bans under Egyptian criminal tax procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting related-party transactions above EGP 8 million with an offshore procurement company without a Local File, no economic role of the related party, or guaranteeing a fixed margin inconsistent with functions performed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA will reconstruct the transaction under the arm's length standard, deny deductions for undocumented imports/service fees, apply penalty amounts for failure to submit TP documentation and charge the 2% monthly late-payment surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved non-arm's length invoicing may be assessed as responsible persons for collected taxes; in severe cases, fraudulent invoicing leads to criminal tax penalties and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC merely as a booking entity with no employees, premises, inventory or decision-making in Egypt; channelling retail revenue through a zero-tax jurisdiction to avoid 22.5% CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA can recharacterise the arrangement, attribute the full retail profit to the Egyptian LLC, deny treaty benefits, impose 22.5% CIT plus penalties, and withhold at 20% on any amount treated as a technical fee or royalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because the corporate form is abused, veil piercing is available; directors can be held jointly liable for the tax gap and may face travel bans and deportation/residence restrictions in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing substantial Cash-on-Delivery receipts through personal bank cards, accepting third-party Stripe/PayPal accounts without beneficiary identification, or failing to keep AML/KYC records for retail distributors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law 80/2002 sanctions inadequate AML controls, typically fines and imprisonment up to five years for deliberate money laundering; settlement accounts may be frozen by CBE and platform payouts paused.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face criminal prosecution, personal fines, and seizure of assets; bank mandates and travel restrictions may be ordered in pending AML investigations.
